transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good afternoon, thank you for calling S-Net Mobile Billing Support. My name is Eleanor. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Eleanor, my name is Persephone. I have just opened my October S-Net mobile bill and I have been charged sixty-two pounds for EU roaming in France when I haven't even left England!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand how frustrating it is to get hit with French roaming charges when you haven't even left Kent or the UK coast, and I am really sorry for the shock of seeing an extra sixty-two pounds on your bill.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you, yes, I was actually hiking along the Kent coast near Dover last weekend, and I certainly didn't cross the Channel!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So just to make sure I have understood the situation properly: while you were walking along the Kent coastline near Dover, your handset inadvertently latched onto a French mobile mast across the Channel and billed you sixty-two pounds in accidental EU roaming charges, is that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that is exactly what happened! It shows two daily EU Roaming Passes plus out-of-bundle maritime and French data charges.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before I open your itemized roaming call data records, could you please confirm your full residential address and your four-digit security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Of course, my address is 27 Castle Hill Road, Dover, Kent, CT16 1QG, and my four-digit PIN is 3106.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for verifying your address and PIN. I have your S-Net Mobile account open in front of me now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great. I am using a Samsung Galaxy S24 that I bought from S-Net in May, and I never touched any roaming settings while I was out walking.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me ask a few questions to verify the cell-tower logs for the credit review. Which exact dates were you walking along the cliffs when those charges triggered?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It was last Saturday the tenth of October and Sunday the eleventh of October.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And where specifically along the coast were you walking on Saturday and Sunday when your phone picked up the foreign signal?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: We walked the White Cliffs path from Dover Eastern Docks up to St Margaret's Bay and the South Foreland Lighthouse on both afternoons.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: St Margaret's Bay is the closest point to Calais, which explains the signal overlap. Did you receive any automated 'Welcome to France' roaming text messages during your walk?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Well, my phone was in my rucksack while I was using a hiking map app, and when I pulled it out at the lighthouse I saw two texts saying 'Welcome to France — £3.50 daily pass activated'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And was your handset's network selection mode set to 'Automatic', with Data Roaming switched on in your mobile connection settings?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, both Network Selection and Data Roaming were left on Automatic from when I went to Spain in July.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Did you make or receive any voice calls or send any photo messages while you were up near the South Foreland Lighthouse on Sunday afternoon?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I sent five photos of the cliffs to my sister on WhatsApp and two standard MMS picture messages to my mum because she doesn't have WhatsApp.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Wait a moment, I am opening the roaming CDR billing table for the tenth and eleventh of October on my screen.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, I have the roaming ledger open now. On Saturday the tenth of October at 14:12 your SIM registered on Bouygues Telecom France (MCC 208 / MNC 20) and triggered a £3.50 EU pass, plus a £42.50 Channel Maritime satellite data session from a passing ferry repeater.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: A forty-two pound fifty ferry satellite session?! I was standing on dry land on the chalk cliffs at St Margaret's Bay, not on a cross-Channel ferry!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Maritime satellite cells on ferries operating in the Dover Strait aren't covered by the EU Roaming Pass cap, so background map data on satellite carrier 901-18 bills at eight pounds fifty per megabyte.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Eight pounds fifty a megabyte when I am standing on an English footpath is daylight robbery!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And then on Sunday the eleventh of October at 15:04 your phone attached to Orange France and billed another £3.50 EU pass plus £12.50 in picture-message and data increments, bringing the total to sixty-two pounds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is crazy! How can S-Net let a French mast and a ferry transmitter hijack my phone while I am walking in my own hometown in Kent?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Honestly, French carrier signal bleed across the Channel isn't our network's problem—Bouygues Telecom boosts their coastal transmitters and there's nothing S-Net can do about foreign radio waves.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Excuse me? I pay S-Net every month for a UK mobile service! Telling a Dover resident that cross-Channel signal bleed isn't your network's problem is a bit much when S-Net is the one billing me sixty-two pounds!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What I mean is that S-Net does not control the transmission power of French masts in Calais or maritime repeaters on ferries in the Strait of Dover.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Maybe not, but S-Net controls its own billing system and can clearly see my phone was connected to a Dover town mast ten minutes before and ten minutes after!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, looking at your domestic cell-site log, your SIM was connected to S-Net cell site DVR-04 in Dover at 14:01, jumped to Bouygues France and the maritime cell at 14:12, and re-attached to Dover mast DVR-07 at 15:18.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Exactly—unless I own a supersonic speedboat, it is physically impossible for me to have gone to France and back in an hour! So you need to wipe that sixty-two pounds off my bill.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And on Sunday your SIM pinged Dover Castle mast DVR-02 at 14:49 and re-attached to St Margaret's mast DVR-09 at 15:35.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, so your own mast logs prove beyond doubt that I never left Kent on either day.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Because the domestic cell-tower ping proves continuous presence in Kent on both dates, our Coastal Inadvertent Roaming policy does cover a full sixty-two pound refund.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good! And can you also put a block on my account so my phone never connects to French or ferry masts again when I walk the dog on the cliffs?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, I can activate a network-level 'UK Domestic Only — Border Roaming Bar' on your SIM profile, and we should also lock your phone onto S-Net manually.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes please, let's do both of those.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Which make and model of phone are you using so I can tell you where the manual network selection menu is?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Eleanor, I already told you two minutes into the call that I am using a Samsung Galaxy S24 that I bought from S-Net in May!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, yes, a Samsung Galaxy S24. Now let me key in the three separate credit lines for the two £3.50 EU passes, the £42.50 maritime data charge, and the £12.50 Sunday data charge.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Please make sure the VAT is included in the credit as well—Wait, are you crediting the full sixty-two pounds in one go or splitting it—

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If you'd stop interrupting me every five seconds I might actually finish adding the credit to your bill.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Pardon me?! There is no need to snap at me like that! I was only asking if the sixty-two pound figure included the VAT!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The sixty-two pound figure already includes VAT. Hold on, I need to apply the credit override code on the coastal roaming ledger now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Fine, go ahead.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, I have posted the full sixty-two pound Coastal Inadvertent Roaming adjustment onto your S-Net Mobile account under credit reference CRM-552910.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You disappeared in silence again for nearly fifty seconds without warning me, Eleanor, though I am glad the sixty-two pound credit is finally put through.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The coastal roaming credit tool has to validate all four call-data-record lines against the Dover mast timestamps before generating reference CRM-552910.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, and what was my total October bill balance before you applied that sixty-two pound credit, and what is it now?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your October bill was eighty-four pounds and zero pence, made up of your twenty-two pound monthly plan plus the sixty-two pounds in roaming charges. Your payable balance is now down to exactly twenty-two pounds and zero pence.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: When my direct debit goes out on the twenty-fifth of October, will it definitely only take twenty-two pounds from my bank account?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, because your direct debit collection file isn't exported to BACS until five working days before the twenty-fifth, the amended twenty-two pound balance is what will be collected.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me open my My S-Net app on my Samsung right now and refresh the billing screen to make sure it says twenty-two pounds.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Go ahead and pull down on the main dashboard screen in the My S-Net app to refresh the live balance.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Refreshing it now... yes! The current balance due on the twenty-fifth of October has just dropped from eighty-four pounds to twenty-two pounds and zero pence, and it lists 'Coastal Roaming Credit -£62.00'!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good, that confirms adjustment CRM-552910 has settled against your October direct debit instruction.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Now, have you also put that network-level Border Roaming Bar onto my SIM card so it blocks French and maritime towers?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, I have just enabled the 'Roam-Bar EU & Maritime' flag on your S-Net HLR subscriber profile. If you ever travel abroad on holiday in future, you can toggle it back on inside the My S-Net app.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And does that network bar block both the French land masts like Bouygues and Orange and the cross-Channel ferry satellite cells?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, it blocks all non-UK PLMN carrier codes, including French terrestrial networks 208-01 and 208-20 as well as maritime satellite network 901-18.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And can you quickly tell me how to switch my Samsung Galaxy S24 from Automatic network selection to manual S-Net UK as an extra safeguard?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: On your Samsung Galaxy S24, open Settings, tap Connections, tap Mobile Networks, and then tap Network Operators.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I am in Mobile Networks and tapping Network Operators now... and I see the toggle that says 'Select automatically'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Slide 'Select automatically' to Off, wait a few seconds for the list of nearby carriers to scan, and tap 'S-Net UK' so your handset never roams onto Bouygues or Orange even if our signal dips.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It is scanning the networks now... funny enough I can actually see 'F-Bouygues' right at the bottom of the list even from my living room in Dover!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That shows how far the Calais coastal transmitters reach across the water on a clear day. Tap 'S-Net UK' at the top of that list.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Done! I have selected S-Net UK manually and it says 'Registered on network — S-Net UK only'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And while you are still in the Mobile Networks menu on your Samsung, also slide the 'Data Roaming' toggle to Off so background apps can never use foreign data.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Just switched Data Roaming to Off as well.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That double lock—manual network selection on the handset plus the network-level roaming bar on your SIM—guarantees you will never get another accidental cross-Channel charge while walking in Dover.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is a relief, because I walk that St Margaret's Bay cliff path almost every weekend.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have also sent an automated email receipt for the sixty-two pound credit CRM-552910 and confirmation of the roaming bar to your email address.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, the confirmation email just popped up on my screen now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else you need me to check on your October mobile bill today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, my bill is back down to my normal twenty-two pounds and the roaming block is active, so that is everything sorted.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You are welcome. Enjoy your weekend walks along the coast, and have a good afternoon. Goodbye!

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Bye now.
